Both link forms have been confirmed to work. The raw.githubusercontent.com links were downloaded and returned 200, with byte sizes that match the catalogue exactly. The via CDN links could not be checked from the environment that generated this page —there, cdn.jsdelivr.net has egress blocked—, so they were composed according to the URL form documented by jsDelivr, and the owner tested one by hand on 2026-09-20. Both are kept: one costs this project nothing to serve, and a reader who finds one of them unavailable still has the other.

INGESTED COPY — this is not WHO and is not live. This page is generated by {folioAssistant} from its own catalogue of {iris}, modelled by reference: {figures}. The WHO logo is deliberately omitted, and the generated covers are not shown for the same reason: they carry the emblem printed on the publications.
Ingested replica. Generated from {catalogue} by {generator}. Design based on {iris}; every figure on this page is read from the catalogue, not copied from a screenshot.

No Dublin Core record. The catalogue states this instead of synthesizing metadata from the PDF: rule R8 of the iris-dspace skill, never infer metadata from the PDF when a record exists, whose converse is that an absent record stays absent.

This is the entrance gate, not the library viewer. The full viewer of library/ is task jbx2 and is being built separately. This page imitates the IRIS home page and links out to other pages, instead of becoming a second answer to the same question.

Three routes to one same item, and that is the idea. The catalogue knows this item only once; the bytes are accessible at source at WHO, here as a replica page and from a CDN node; jsDelivr serves any public repository, so the last one costs this project no hosting. The knowledge graph says what exists and where; the CDN says nothing and simply serves it.

Where the held copies really are — task yl5w. The catalogue records each of them at uploads/<name>.pdf relative to who-iris/, and all three paths are missing: #477 moved library/ to this instance and left uploads/ in cat-harness/.

The download links above point to where the bytes are, so they work. What is wrong is the catalogue's claim, and check:catalogue does not check localPath at all: it verifies metadataRef and libraryId, and accepts as good a run over three materialized claims that point to nothing.
The interface is shown in {language}. Titles, authors, abstracts and other catalogue records are shown as WHO published them.

The main objective of the Institutional Repository for Information Sharing (IRIS) is to provide free digital access to the scientific and technical publications of the World Health Organization (WHO), including the contributions of its country offices, its regional offices and Headquarters. In addition, IRIS encompasses the mandates established by the Organization's governing bodies in collaboration with its Member States.
